text:
yael: quick sanity ping — brought up a converted Mistral->Gemma build and seeing ~+6% chrF loss on a short summarization set vs upstream. latency fine but hallucinating dates and mis-attributing years.

yael: initial hunch: rotary frequency or head scaling interaction during conversion. converter flags were `--preserve-rotary` but loader applies headwise scaling by default.

tomas: paste the eval command and conversion args?

yael: reproducer: `python eval.py --model /mnt/models/zephyr-gemma/ --task summarization --quant=int4 --batch=1`
flags used: `--from=mistral --to=gemma --preserve-rotary --headwise-scale=yes`

nina: also check tokenizer mapping. small shifts in special token ids (BOS/EOS) frequently change behaviour — seen similar hallucination patterns from token-id misalignments.

yael: ran token spot-check: token id for "2023" changed (50257 upstream vs 50256 converted).

samir: that suggests a vocab-offset combined with rotary misalignment. If token ids shift, KV cache indices and rotary angle indexing can point to wrong sin/cos pairs.

yael: logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-21T14:12:01Z] model_load: rotor_map applied headwise_scale=True
[2026-03-21T14:12:02Z] vocab_map: offset=+1 applied (preserve_specials=False)
[2026-03-21T14:12:02Z] eval: chrF=0.623 -> 0.586
```

tomas: try two quick variants: A) re-convert with `--preserve-specials` enabled, B) at load time set `rotary_head_scale: disable` and re-eval.

yael: running both now, will report back.

triage-bot: Note: opened issue INFR-214 "rotary/headwise scaling conversion mismatches"

nina: additionally diff the per-head rotary frequency arrays between upstream and converted weights; tiny fractional differences (0.999 vs 1.0) blow up on long contexts.

samir: mitigation idea: during conversion, remap and lock special token ids (BOS/EOS/PAD) before applying any global offset; we've got a 2025 patch that does exactly this.

yael: quick results: re-convert with `--preserve-specials` restored many token ids and chrF rose to 0.617. disabling headwise scaling at load time yielded chrF 0.622 (within noise of upstream). latency unchanged.

yael: root cause looks like a two-part failure: converter applied +1 offset to non-special tokens while preserve_specials=False, and our serving loader defaulted to headwise scaling. Together they amplified semantic drift.

tomas: solid find. action items: 1) change converter default to preserve specials, 2) add a conversion-time sanity check that compares token ids for numerals/punctuation/common tokens, 3) make loader emit a warning when headwise scaling is active for converted models.

samir: I'll draft a PR with the sanity check and unit tests for token-id invariants.

nina: I'll quarantine the converted artifact in the model catalog, update the onboarding checklist to include a token-id diff step and rotary-array compare.

yael: will re-run the full eval after PR merges. cc @tomas — can you add a tiny build hook to log rotary arrays during conversion builds?

tomas: yes, will add a smoke step: compare the top-10 frequent token ids and compute L2 norm between upstream/converted rotary freq arrays. if norms > threshold, fail conversion.

triage-bot: INFR-214 updated: labels [onboarding, rotary, vocab] added.

yael: note for the team: if you see similar small chrF deltas elsewhere, flag immediately. symptom rarely catastrophic on its face but correlates with hallucination risk.

samir: PR created: converter/#432 — includes preserve-specials default toggle and token-id diff test.

nina: catalog entry updated and artifact marked quarantine until reconversion.

yael: will post final chrF numbers once full eval done. thanks all :thumbsup:
